solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It comes off with cloth initially?

definitions.text: It comes off with cloth initially?

indicators.note: off means the two words go wrong, coming out in a new order
initially means just the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A riddle about something removed when a cloth is first applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges IT COMES; 'initially' adds the C of cloth. Read whole, the clue describes make-up, wiped away with a cleansing cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Face make-up is the thing a cleansing cloth wipes away, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Witness royal couple perhaps after using smallest room

indicators.note: after places the royal couple's letters behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: someone 'on' a drug is using it
the smallest room is a jokey name for the toilet, the loo
K (king) and ER (queen, Elizabeth Regina) make a royal pair

explanation.surface: A royal pair seen emerging after a visit to the toilet, as told by a witness.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; K is the chess and card abbreviation for king.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander who sees something happen is a witness to it.

clue.text: Island on the brink of success ejects one socialite

parts.note: the Isle of Man, often just Man

indicators.note: ejects means the phrase throws one letter out of itself

parts.note: on the brink of success is being about to win
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An island society figure, nearly winning, throws someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejects' takes I out of ABOUT TO WIN, leaving ABOUT TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable figure seen at all the fashionable parties is a familiar phrase for a socialite.

clue.text: Suppress, informally, finished Times article by its Paris correspondent?

parts.note: finished is through, informally shortened to thro'
T for time, twice
the French counterpart of the definite article is le

explanation.surface: A wry question about the Times printing an article written by its Paris reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is T (time) twice, not the newspaper; the Paris 'correspondent' of an article is the French word le.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle or choke something off is to suppress it.

clue.text: Till operator to take out of service

definitions.meaning: the person at a shop or bank counter handling money
to dismiss an officer from the armed forces in disgrace

explanation.surface: A checkout worker fired from the job.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the shop's money handler, the other the military verb for dishonourable discharge.

clue.text: Designer's month in Paris, hosting bishop

definitions.note: Designer's reads as 'designer is', so the definition is the noun designer

indicators.note: hosting means the French word holds the bishop's letters within it

parts.note: the French word for month is mois
RR, Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's month spent in Paris with a bishop as guest.
explanation.walkthrough: William Morris was the Victorian textile and wallpaper designer.
explanation.definitionFit: William Morris, Arts and Crafts pioneer, is a famous English pattern designer.

clue.text: Address to Athenians using Zeno's place

indicators.note: using means the answer is drawn from letters in the preceding words

explanation.surface: A speech to the people of Athens given at the philosopher Zeno's venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Address', all of 'to' and the start of 'Athenians'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Citium taught in the painted colonnade in Athens, giving the Stoics their name.

clue.text: Bond's nemesis all but capturing revolutionary plotters

indicators.note: capturing means the shortened agency holds the revolutionary inside
all but means the last letter of the agency is dropped

parts.note: SMERSH, the Soviet counter-intelligence agency in Ian Fleming's novels
Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: James Bond's foe seizes a rebel, a natural spy-story plot.
explanation.walkthrough: SMERSH is the Soviet spy agency James Bond fights in Ian Fleming's novels; 'all but' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who scheme are conspirators who plot.

clue.text: A dreamer, withholding name, giving out bouquet

indicators.note: withholding means the word keeps back one of its letters

parts.note: an idealistic dreamer is a romantic

explanation.surface: A dreamy person, keeping their name back, hands out a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks like flowers but here is a wine's scent; 'withholding' removes N from ROMANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fragrant that gives off a pleasant scent is described as aromatic.

clue.text: Last to leave side dish

indicators.note: last to leave means the word's final letter goes

parts.note: the flank is the side of an animal or army

explanation.surface: A dinner guest is the last to leave, with a side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling is a type of dish.

clue.text: Could it be cheap later on? Not this house

indicators.note: the question suggests these letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a property will be cheaper later, before deciding against this house.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament, members of the Commons traditionally call the House of Lords 'another place' rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliamentary custom has each chamber refer to the other obliquely, so it means the house that is not this one.

clue.text: Left Janet dancing with Andrew, prominently featured?

indicators.note: dancing means the two names jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: Janet left the floor after dancing with Andrew, who has striking features.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, jutting jaw gives a face a prominent feature, the jokey sense of the definition.

clue.text: Make last European king veto cult, ignoring the odds

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means only the even-placed letters are kept

explanation.surface: A European monarch bans a sect, defying the odds, to make his reign endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch a small supply so it goes further is to make it last.

clue.text: The Spanish cross about one New Zealand port

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: about means the angry word goes round the other letters

parts.note: cross means angry, or sore
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Spanish speaker annoyed about one port in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Zealand' looks like the country, but New gives N and Zealand is the Danish island where Hamlet's castle town stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore (Helsingør) is a harbour town on Zealand, the largest island of Denmark.

clue.text: Harnessed mount runs into rock

indicators.note: into means the runs go inside the word for rock

parts.note: to rock unsteadily is to totter
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A horse in harness bolts into a boulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse bred for harness racing, pulling a sulky, is a trotter.

clue.text: In plane maybe a model picked up paper

indicators.note: in means the following pieces sit inside the word for a plane

parts.note: a plane is an example of a tree

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: Someone on an aircraft picks up a model's newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the tree, not an aircraft; 'picked up' reads the model's word upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly paper or essay on a subject is a treatise.

clue.text: They pinch what's close to me, coming round the night before

indicators.note: coming round means the near-pointing word goes around the other

parts.note: 'this' points at something near the speaker, unlike 'that'
eve, the evening before a festival

explanation.surface: Pickpockets operating close to someone the evening before an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points at what is near the speaker, as against 'that'; 'coming round' wraps it about the eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinch is slang for steal, so those who pinch are robbers.

clue.text: Women's entertaining a bar with a dance

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the following pieces as guests inside

parts.note: Hera, goddess of women and marriage, is women's patron
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A women's group entertains a bar crowd with a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hera, wife of Zeus, was the Greek goddess of women.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a Cuban dance in slow duple time, famous from Carmen.

clue.text: Astronomer looks into this segment of big wheel?

indicators.note: of puts the segment after the wheel, as in a wheel's piece

parts.note: the London Eye, the giant observation wheel on the Thames
a segment is a piece

explanation.surface: An astronomer peers into a section of a big wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The lens at the viewing end of a telescope is what an observer puts an eye to.

clue.text: Lead choking dog? Make haste slowly, perhaps

indicators.note: choking means the symbol for the metal is wrapped round the dog

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover, a stock dog's name

explanation.surface: A leash strangling a dog, so perhaps the walk should be slower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a dog's leash but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Make haste slowly' is an old saying, an example of a maxim.

clue.text: Relief worker, abrasive, short, guvnor roped in

indicators.note: roped in means the boss is enclosed by the shortened abrasive
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: emery is an abrasive powder used on emery boards
guv'nor is slang for the boss

explanation.surface: An aid worker with a rough manner, short with the boss who drafted them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' is raised design, not aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised relief designs on metal or paper are made by a craftsman who stamps them.

clue.text: Small time criminal cases rear of factory block

indicators.note: cases means the rearranged letters enclose another
criminal means the letters of the word are crooked, out of order
rear of means the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A minor crook breaks into the back of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TIME to TMIE, which 'cases' round Y (rear of factory) to give TYMIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie someone is to obstruct or thwart them.

clue.text: Censor advocates touring square without one

indicators.note: touring means going round the other letters

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers, or advocates

indicators.note: without means the square loses a letter

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A censor and a group of lawyers go round a public square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' is not a town square but nine, a square number.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor is someone who prohibits things, one who bans.

clue.text: Stoker's place in rail van: nasty when shunted

indicators.note: shunted means the letters are pushed into a new arrangement, like railway wagons

explanation.surface: A railway fireman stoking an engine in a nasty, shunted rail van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoker' is Bram Stoker, author of Dracula, not a railway fireman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker set Count Dracula's castle in this region of Romania.

clue.text: Scrap half the alphabet

definitions.meaning: a tiny particle, the smallest bit of anything
read as letters, the first half of the alphabet runs from A to M

explanation.surface: Throw away half the letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a tiny particle or iota; the other reads A-to-M, letters one to thirteen.

clue.text: Got rid of water plant in the wrong place?

definitions.meaning: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted

explanation.surface: A gardener removed a water plant growing in the wrong spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's unwanted plant, and also the past tense of the childish word for urinating.

clue.text: Pair row, following poles — more stuck up

indicators.note: following puts these pieces after the poles

parts.note: S and N, the south and north poles
in cricket a pair is two noughts, a duck in each innings
a row of seats is a tier

explanation.surface: A pair of rowers, coming after the polar explorers, look more haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'pair' is being out for nought in both innings, written as two zeros.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooty means haughty, so its comparative means more snobbish.

clue.text: Mint drink, with note in it

indicators.note: in it means the pieces go inside the drink

parts.note: a brew is a drink, especially tea or beer
with means and

explanation.surface: A mint drink with a note slipped into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the herb but means in perfect new condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint condition means pristine, as fresh as when new.
